scope: Whole aux_funcs.py (427 lines) and tee.py read; direct calls to unchanged original auxiliary functions under bundled Python 3.
findings: get_next_entry assumes len(read(blocksize)) < blocksize means EOF. A seekable BytesIO-derived reader limited to four bytes per read truncates a six-byte entry to two bytes. This is a general stream-contract counterexample, not evidence that regular disk reads always truncate.
Experimental size-grouping helpers retain Python 2 xrange/iteritems; direct ordinary Python 3 calls fail as recorded. Current production reachability outside reviewed rfigc is not established.
recwalk supplies no onerror callback to os.walk/scandir.walk and exposes only discovered files, without explicit omission diagnostics or traversal budgets.
copy_any removes destination before checking whether source exists when only_missing is false. Not executed: no destructive helper called.
Tee.close suppresses flush exceptions; log durability is not confirmed by successful close. Not an application database write guarantee.
